extracted.intended_audience: judge advocates, convening and reviewing military commanders, and other military legal officers responsible for courts-martial records and review
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards governing the preparation, authentication, promulgation, review, validity, and possible defects of court-martial proceedings and sentences, and the authority of reviewing/approving officers (including the President and Secretaries) to act on them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretion in severity of reprimand
rubrics_metrics.description: Although a reprimand is generally intended to impose a mild punishment, the quality (severity) of the reprimand is left to the discretion of the authority pronouncing it and may be made as severe as he deems expedient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authority who pronounces a reprimand is not chargeable with adding to a punishment by making the reprimand severe. (R. 33, 498, Nov., 1872.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of commander approval for certain non-dismissal punishments
rubrics_metrics.description: When a court-martial convened by a department commander sentences an officer to loss of files or steps in the list of officers of his rank, the approval of the convening commander is sufficient to give full effect to the sentence; no superior action is required to add to its effect or conclusiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike dismissal sentences, confirmation by the President is not essential to execution of such punishments; the commander should notify the Secretary of War by forwarding a copy of the promulgating order. Proceedings (or their substance) affecting other officers may be republished in Adjutant General's orders. (R. 36, 134, Dec., 1874; 37, 83, Oct., 1875; 43, 286, Apr., 1880.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Record must show reviewing action
rubrics_metrics.description: The record should exhibit, at the end of the court proceedings, the action taken thereon (approval, disapproval, etc.) by the reviewing authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although sometimes indorsed on the outside, it is preferable and customary that the reviewing officer's action be written and signed within the record on a page following the authenticated judgment. Where several cases are tried by the same court, the reviewing officer's action should be entered in the record of each trial; merely indorsing it upon the last of a series is irregular. A mere reference that the record was 'forwarded' for action is incomplete — the original reviewing officer should state his approval etc. in full and formal terms. (R. 2, 650, June, 1863; R.4, 428, Dec., 1863; R. 19, 336, Jan., 1866; R. 41, 337, Nov., 1863; 7, 132, Feb., 1864; O., 2844, Jan., 1897.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of reviewing authority's action (signature and rank)
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewing authority should authenticate his action by subscribing in his own hand the official statement as written in or upon the record and should add his rank and command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impressing the signature by stamp is not favored. (R. 4t 567, Jan., 1864; 22, 513, Dec., 1866, and 568, Jan., 1867.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Release pending review when acquitted or no confinement
rubrics_metrics.description: When a court-martial results in an acquittal or the sentence contains no confinement, the prisoner may, pending review of the proceedings, be released from confinement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of promulgation must reflect reviewing action date
rubrics_metrics.description: The sentence should commence on the date of the action taken by the reviewing authority; therefore the date of that action should appear in the promulgating order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is often not practicable for special orders but when possible the promulgation date should match the reviewing authority's action. (C. 1681, Aug. 1891.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Promulgation not essential to validity if action indorsed
rubrics_metrics.description: An order of promulgation is a convenient means of communicating proceedings but is not necessary to the validity of proceedings or sentence provided the reviewing authority's official action is duly indorsed upon or appended to the record and notice is given to the affected party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when no promulgating order is issued, proceedings and sentences will be formally complete and operative if the action of the reviewing authority is properly indorsed and notice given. (R. 32, 102, Nov., 1871; C. 1226, Apr., 1895; 3810, Jan. 27, 1898; 12623, May 26, 1902.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Officer authorized to act on sentence should promulgate proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The officer authorized to act upon the sentence is the proper authority to promulgate by order the proceedings of the court and his action thereon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the regiment of the accused is outside the command at promulgation date, a copy of the order should be forwarded to the commanding officer of the accused. (C. 5235, Nov., 1898.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to recommit mistakenly released prisoners
rubrics_metrics.description: A department commander by whom a sentence has been approved is legally authorized to order a soldier who was mistakenly released before completing his legal term to be recommitted to complete the punishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: President as final reviewing authority for certain sentences
rubrics_metrics.description: For sentences of dismissal and of death imposed in time of peace (and some wartime death sentences) and all sentences affecting general officers, the President is the final reviewing officer when the sentence must be confirmed by the President under applicable articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The convening officer (or successor) may be the original reviewing authority. Once the President has acted, his function as reviewing or confirming authority is exhausted and his approval or disapproval, once notified to the accused, is beyond his power to revise or modify thereafter except by pardon. (Articles 105–109; R. 9, 44, May, 1864; 38, 104, June, 1876; 42, 91, Dec., 1878.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of confirmation by President not prescribed
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 106 does not require the President's personal signature nor prescribe a form for confirmation; a written approval authenticated by the Secretary of War (or expressed to be by his order) is sufficient as confirmation within the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where personal signature is not made essential by law, the head of the department's signature is sufficient, the President's assent to his order being presumed. (R. 9, 44, May, 1864; P. 22, 436, Feb., 1888.)

rubrics_metrics.name: War Department lacks authority to correct findings or add to sentence
rubrics_metrics.description: The War Department has no authority to correct the findings or sentence of a court-martial or to add to the sentence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing authority may express disapproval/censure in review
rubrics_metrics.description: When taking action on a case, the reviewing authority may formally express disapprobation of the court's neglect to do its duty, even if such remarks might be interpreted as censure or reprimand of the accused.

rubrics_metrics.name: New/second trials permissible only in limited circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: New or second trials are authorized only when the reviewing authority disapproves the original sentence and the accused asks for a second trial; the privilege is discretionary, not a right, and after a sentence has been duly approved and taken effect a new trial is beyond the power of a military commander or the President.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically rare; early Attorney General opinion held that if accused requests a new trial the double-jeopardy bar does not apply because the objection is waived by consent. (R. 37, 492, Apr., 1876; 39, 233, Oct., 1877; 43, 423, and 44, 171, Oct., 1880; C. 5654, July 24, 1899.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Records need not prove every technical item (e.g., expenditures) to be sustained
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical requirements such as showing proof of all expenditures by the Government in the record (to sustain reimbursement items in a sentence) would unduly hamper military justice; disapproval for such technical defects cannot be concurred in by the department (i.e., such technical omissions are not grounds to invalidate sentence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: disapproval of sentence because amount items not proved was not supported; C. 1876 4-A, Nov. 23, 1909.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counsel access subordinate to service interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasonable facilities for procuring counsel should be afforded an accused but the accused's claim is subordinate to the interests of the service; a commander may deny a particular counsel request if that officer cannot be spared without material prejudice to public interests and the legality of proceedings is not affected by such denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption in favor of jurisdiction and regularity
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless it clearly appears to the contrary on the face of the record, it is generally presumed that the court had jurisdiction and the proceedings were sufficiently regular to be valid in law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although many defects were common historically, generally only irremediable or vital defects (e.g., court composed of fewer than minimum members) render proceedings inoperative; minor form defects should not generally be held fatal if sufficient appears to warrant presumption of compliance or the reviewing authority can supply defects from official knowledge or evidence. (R. 12, 353, Feb., 1865; G. 16101, Apr. 21, 1904.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction: substantive vs judicial portions of record
rubrics_metrics.description: The court record consists of substantive (attestation of proceedings and acts) and judicial portions; the substantive portion is attributed unerring verity and cannot be contradicted except by production of the record itself or properly certified copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supreme Court holdings establish that a court-martial's recorded acts are judicial proceedings and the record cannot be lawfully altered or impeached by outside affidavits. Example: sentence executed and later affidavits claiming missing witness testimony could not contradict the record. (C. 5654, July, 1899.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Irregular referral of charges not necessarily fatal
rubrics_metrics.description: Charges irregularly referred to a court-martial by an inferior commander without approval of the convening officer do not necessarily affect the validity of proceedings or sentence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irregular convening order date not material
rubrics_metrics.description: An order convening a court dated on a Sunday does not affect the validity of proceedings tried under that order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor errors in description of members not material if identification sufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: Erroneous statement of the regiment or corps of a member of the court or the judge advocate is not a material objection to validity provided the description is sufficient to identify the officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to include article 100 direction does not vitiate dismissal
rubrics_metrics.description: Though article 100's direction to be added to the sentence should regularly be complied with, failure to do so will not affect the validity of a dismissal sentence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record must affirmatively show statutory essentials of jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: The record must affirmatively show whatever statute makes essential to jurisdiction and legality of proceedings (e.g., that members and the judge advocate were sworn).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the record fails to show required statutory acts (like swearing) and the omission cannot be supplied by revision, the sentence may be void. However, if the court has not been dissolved the reviewing authority or successor may reconvene the court to supply omissions in the record to make it speak the truth. (R. 1, 487, Dec., 1862; many others.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation by relieved member is fatal
rubrics_metrics.description: If an officer detailed as a member of a general court-martial was duly relieved by order but nevertheless continued to sit, participate in findings and sentence, the sentence should be set aside as null and void.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unauthorized substitution of judge advocate is fatal
rubrics_metrics.description: If a court excused its judge advocate and required its junior member to act as judge advocate, that action is wholly unauthorized and the proceedings should be disapproved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the convening authority can relieve or detail a member or judge advocate. (R. 28, 198, Oct., 1868.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery of fatal defect after approval may permit supplemental order
rubrics_metrics.description: Where, after the reviewing commander had approved a sentence and the court had been dissolved, a fatal defect is discovered in the proceedings, the commander may issue a supplemental order declaring the proceedings nullity and withdraw the original order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal to accept accused's written statement is fatal
rubrics_metrics.description: A court-martial has no authority to abridge the accused's right to submit a written statement; refusal to receive such a written statement renders the proceedings fatally defective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to make any finding on the charge is fatal
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a fatal defect for a court-martial not to make any finding on the charge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence by court without jurisdiction is void
rubrics_metrics.description: A sentence awarded by a court which was without jurisdiction is void and cannot operate to separate a soldier from the service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: soldier remained in volunteer service until muster-out date and his status at separation was that of a soldier in confinement under charges. (C. 13103, Aug. 7, 1902.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceedings void when convening order is null and void
rubrics_metrics.description: Court-martial proceedings are void when the order assuming to convene the court is null and void.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record failing to show swearing of members/judge advocate is fatally defective
rubrics_metrics.description: A record which fails to show that the members of the court and the judge advocate were duly sworn is fatally defective; affidavits by judge advocate and president on revision do not remedy the defect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such fatal defects require setting aside sentence and recalling discharge if dishonorable discharge resulted. (C. 9600, Jan. 9, 1901; 8197, May 3, 1900; 15330, Oct. 14, 1903.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to show opportunity to exercise challenge is fatal
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the record fails to show that the accused was allowed opportunity to exercise his right of challenge, the proceedings are fatally defective and the sentence is void.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omission in charges may be fatal but amendment and retrial possible
rubrics_metrics.description: If essential elements (e.g., alleging receipt of pay/allowances in fraudulent enlistment charge) are omitted, proceedings may be fatally defective as not constituting an offense; however, charges may be amended and the accused retried before a legally constituted court without constituting a second trial for the same offense within the meaning of the statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceedings by court reduced below minimum members are inoperative
rubrics_metrics.description: If a court, reduced by absence of members, operation of challenges, etc., proceeds with fewer than the statutory minimum (five members for a general court-martial), its further proceedings including findings and sentence are unauthorized and inoperative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval null when soldier already discharged
rubrics_metrics.description: Approval of a sentence is null and void when the soldier in question has already been discharged from the service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remission or mitigation for failure of proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Where proof is weak (example: prosecution introduced only one witness who was contradicted on a material point), the reviewing authority may advise that pending execution the unexecuted portion of the sentence be remitted on account of failure of proof.
